question: True or false: goldfish have a memory of only about three seconds.
fact: Experiments show goldfish can remember things for months.

question: True or false: humans use only 10% of their brains.
fact: Brain scans show activity across virtually the whole brain.

question: True or false: botanically speaking, a tomato is a fruit.
fact: Cucumbers, peppers and pumpkins are botanically fruits too.

question: True or false: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain on Earth measured from base to peak.
fact: Mauna Kea in Hawaii is taller when measured from its base on the seafloor.

question: True or false: sound travels faster through water than through air.
fact: Sound moves about four times faster in water than in air.

question: True or false: a group of flamingos can be called a 'flamboyance'.
fact: Flamingos often stand on one leg, even while they sleep.

question: True or false: bananas grow on trees.
fact: The banana plant is a giant herb; its 'trunk' is tightly rolled leaves.

question: True or false: Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short for his time.
fact: He was about 1.69 m, around average for a Frenchman of his era.

question: True or false: Viking warriors wore horned helmets into battle.
fact: Horned Viking helmets were invented by 1800s costume designers.

question: True or false: Cleopatra was of Greek descent.
fact: She belonged to the Ptolemies, a dynasty with roots in Macedonia.

question: True or false: Antarctica is the largest desert in the world.
fact: A desert is defined by how little rain or snow falls, not by heat.

question: True or false: Russia has a larger surface area than the dwarf planet Pluto.
fact: Russia covers about 17.1 million km2; Pluto's surface is about 16.7 million.

question: True or false: the Eiffel Tower can grow taller in summer.
fact: Heat makes its iron expand, adding up to about 15 cm.

question: True or false: sealed honey can stay edible for thousands of years.
fact: Honey's high sugar and low water make it very hard for germs to grow.

question: True or false: sharks are mammals.
fact: Sharks are fish; whales and dolphins are the ocean mammals.

question: True or false: a bolt of lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun.
fact: Lightning can reach around 30,000 C, about five times hotter.

question: True or false: the Pacific is the deepest ocean.
fact: Its Mariana Trench plunges about 11 km below the surface.

question: True or false: Shakespeare wrote his plays in Old English.
fact: He wrote in Early Modern English; Old English is the language of Beowulf.

question: True or false: cheetahs can roar like lions.
fact: Cheetahs purr, chirp and hiss, but they cannot roar.

question: True or false: ostriches bury their heads in the sand when scared.
fact: They lower their heads to turn their eggs, which sit in holes in the ground.

question: True or false: on average, Mercury is the closest planet to Earth.
fact: Because it hugs the Sun, Mercury is on average the nearest planet to every other planet.

question: True or false: old windows are thicker at the bottom because glass slowly flows.
fact: Old glass was simply made unevenly, and fitters put the thick edge down.

question: True or false: bulls get angry at the colour red.
fact: Bulls are red-green colourblind; it is the cape's movement that provokes them.

question: True or false: perfectly pure water is a good conductor of electricity.
fact: It is the dissolved salts and minerals that make everyday water conductive.

question: True or false: Albert Einstein failed maths at school.
fact: Einstein had mastered calculus by the age of about 15.

question: True or false: Mount Kilimanjaro is in Kenya.
fact: Kilimanjaro is in Tanzania, close to the Kenyan border.

question: True or false: Brazil is the only South American country with Portuguese as its official language.
fact: Spanish dominates elsewhere; Guyana uses English and Suriname Dutch.

question: True or false: Sweden and Norway share a land border.
fact: Their border is one of the longest in Europe, over 1,600 km.

question: True or false: there are more trees on Earth than stars in the Milky Way.
fact: Earth has about 3 trillion trees; the galaxy has perhaps 100 to 400 billion stars.

question: True or false: koalas are a type of bear.
fact: Koalas are marsupials that carry their young in a pouch.

question: True or false: Pluto was discovered in 1930.
fact: Clyde Tombaugh found it, and an 11-year-old girl suggested the name.

question: True or false: Spain uses the same time zone as Poland.
fact: Spain switched to Central European Time in 1940.

question: True or false: most wild lions live in dense jungle.
fact: Lions live mainly in open savanna and grassland.

question: True or false: the Moon has no gravity.
fact: The Moon's gravity is about one sixth of Earth's.

question: True or false: astronauts float on the space station because there is no gravity there.
fact: Gravity there is about 90% of Earth's; they float because they are in free fall.

question: True or false: early humans lived at the same time as Tyrannosaurus rex.
fact: T. rex died out about 66 million years before modern humans appeared.

question: True or false: the Mona Lisa has no clearly visible eyebrows.
fact: Any eyebrows may have faded or been cleaned away over the centuries.

question: True or false: Ludwig van Beethoven was born in Germany.
fact: He was born in Bonn but spent most of his life in Vienna.

question: True or false: a standard Rubik's Cube has six colours.
fact: Hungarian architect Erno Rubik invented the cube in 1974.

question: True or false: golf has been played on the Moon.
fact: Astronaut Alan Shepard hit two golf balls on the Moon in 1971.

question: True or false: Olympic gold medals are made of solid gold.
fact: They are mostly silver, plated with at least 6 g of gold.

question: True or false: wild penguins live at the North Pole.
fact: Wild penguins live almost entirely in the Southern Hemisphere.

question: True or false: polar bears live in Antarctica.
fact: Polar bears live in the Arctic, so they never meet penguins in the wild.

question: True or false: blood is blue while it is inside your veins.
fact: Blood is always red; veins only look blue through the skin.

question: True or false: fortune cookies were invented in China.
fact: They were popularised in the USA and likely trace back to Japanese crackers.

question: True or false: coffee beans are actually seeds.
fact: They are the seeds of a red, cherry-like fruit.

question: True or false: peanuts are true nuts.
fact: Peanuts are legumes, related to peas and beans, and grow underground.

question: True or false: almonds are close relatives of peaches.
fact: Almonds, peaches, cherries and plums all belong to the Prunus genus.

question: True or false: Mars has the largest known volcano in the solar system.
fact: Olympus Mons on Mars covers an area about the size of Poland.

question: True or false: the Atlantic Ocean is saltier than the Pacific Ocean.
fact: Strong evaporation keeps the Atlantic's surface water saltier.

question: True or false: sound cannot travel through the vacuum of space.
fact: With no air to carry vibrations, explosions in space would be silent.

question: True or false: one Earth year is exactly 365 days long.
fact: It is about 365.25 days, which is why we add leap days.

question: True or false: Earth is closest to the Sun in January.
fact: Seasons are caused by Earth's tilt, not its distance from the Sun.

question: True or false: Hawaii is slowly moving closer to Japan.
fact: The Pacific Plate carries Hawaii north-west by several centimetres a year.

question: True or false: the Amazon River flows into the Pacific Ocean.
fact: The Amazon flows east and pours into the Atlantic Ocean.

question: True or false: the Dead Sea is really a lake.
fact: It is a landlocked salt lake, almost ten times saltier than the ocean.

question: True or false: Leonardo da Vinci painted The Last Supper.
fact: It is a mural on the wall of a convent dining hall in Milan.

question: True or false: ancient Greek marble statues were originally painted in bright colours.
fact: Traces of pigment show that many statues were once brightly coloured.

question: True or false: in Norse mythology, Loki is Thor's brother.
fact: That comes from Marvel; in the myths Loki is Odin's blood brother.

question: True or false: in Greek myth, Medusa's gaze could turn people to stone.
fact: Even her severed head kept the power to turn people to stone.

question: True or false: all sushi contains raw fish.
fact: Sushi means the vinegared rice; many kinds have no fish at all.

question: True or false: the Sun is a star.
fact: The Sun is a fairly ordinary yellow dwarf star.

question: True or false: electrons are bigger than atoms.
fact: Electrons are tiny particles found inside atoms.

question: True or false: fingernails keep growing after a person dies.
fact: The skin dries and pulls back, which only makes the nails look longer.

question: True or false: camels store water in their humps.
fact: A camel's hump stores fat, which it can use for energy.

question: True or false: Venus is the brightest planet in our night sky.
fact: After the Moon, Venus is the brightest natural object in the night sky.

question: True or false: mosquitoes cause more human deaths than any other animal.
fact: Diseases spread by mosquitoes, like malaria, kill hundreds of thousands a year.

question: True or false: some turtles can breathe through their bottoms.
fact: Australia's Fitzroy River turtle absorbs oxygen through its rear end.

question: True or false: Japan is made up of more than 6,000 islands.
fact: A 2023 recount found over 14,000 islands, about double the old figure.

question: True or false: the Great Wall of China is one single continuous wall.
fact: It is many walls built by different dynasties over about 2,000 years.

question: True or false: the Eiffel Tower was meant to be a temporary structure.
fact: It had a 20-year permit and was saved partly because it was useful for radio.

question: True or false: the University of Oxford is older than the Aztec Empire.
fact: Teaching at Oxford began by 1096; Tenochtitlan was founded around 1325.

question: True or false: Marie Antoinette is recorded saying 'Let them eat cake'.
fact: There is no evidence she said it; the story appeared before she was famous.

question: True or false: woolly mammoths were still alive when the Great Pyramid was built.
fact: A small group survived on Wrangel Island until around 2000 BC.

question: True or false: the Sahara has always been a desert.
fact: About 6,000 to 10,000 years ago the Sahara was green, with lakes and grassland.

question: True or false: sodium metal reacts violently when dropped in water.
fact: It can fizz, burst into flame or even explode.

question: True or false: women first competed in the modern Olympics in 1900.
fact: Women took part in events such as tennis and golf at Paris 1900.

question: True or false: in tennis, points in a game go 15, 30, 40.
fact: One popular theory links the numbers to the quarters of a clock face.

question: True or false: basketball was invented by a Canadian.
fact: James Naismith was Canadian, teaching in Massachusetts in 1891.

question: True or false: Sherlock Holmes never says 'Elementary, my dear Watson' in the original stories.
fact: He says 'Elementary' and 'my dear Watson', but never together like that.

question: True or false: in Mary Shelley's novel, the monster is named Frankenstein.
fact: Victor Frankenstein is the scientist; his creature is never given a name.

question: True or false: the first Harry Potter book was rejected by several publishers.
fact: J. K. Rowling's first book was turned down around a dozen times.

question: True or false: Beethoven was completely deaf from birth.
fact: His hearing began to fail in his late twenties.

question: True or false: Nintendo was founded in the 1800s.
fact: Nintendo began in 1889 in Kyoto, making playing cards.

question: True or false: the first computer mouse was made of wood.
fact: Douglas Engelbart's 1960s prototype was a wooden box with two wheels.

question: True or false: Wi-Fi is short for 'wireless fidelity'.
fact: Wi-Fi is just a brand name chosen to sound catchy, like hi-fi.

question: True or false: email existed before the World Wide Web.
fact: The first network email was sent in 1971, about 20 years before the web.
